events.title: James Joyce Walking Tour
events.description: A fun and exciting walking tour of James Joyce's Dublin offered by the James Joyce Centre. Though Joyce lived most of his life outside of Ireland, Dublin would provide the backdrop for virtually all of his work. On a stroll around the inner city, our guide will explain the real-life inspiration behind some of Joyce’s most celebrated writing, demonstrating just how central the streetscape of the ‘Hibernian metropolis’ was to the author’s life and art. The tour visits such stops as Belvedere College, the Gresham Hotel, the James Joyce Statue, Davy Byrnes, and the National Library. This is an excellent and fun introduction to Joyce in a bustling part of the city. Every Thur, Fri & Sat at 11am. Admission to the James Joyce Centre is included.

events.title: Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design
events.description: Our current exhibition at the National Print Museum, Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design, uses flight as a central thread to explore how design and print helped promote Irish modernisation and position Ireland internationally. With the arrival of a number of Dutch graphic designers to Ireland in the 1950s to work on advertising for Aer Lingus, depictions of Ireland and Irishness were forever changed, as was Ireland’s relationship to Continental Europe and the US. Their design work was recognised internationally and had a huge impact on Irish design and economic development. Free admission. events.title: Remembering World War 1 Tour
events.description: Join us at the GPO Museum for this special tour as we remember those involved in World War 1. In September 1914 Europe went over the precipice and war was declared. The people of the island of Ireland were faced with stark choices; join the war effort and support the British Empire, or take the opportunity the war provided to fight for the Ireland they wanted. This guided tour will tell the stories of those Irishmen and women who participated in World War 1, both their actions during the war and their lives afterwards, the effect and role the Irish Revolution had on these individuals, and how they are remembered today, not just in Ireland but in the countries they fought in across Europe.

What do the results tell us about the direction of American politics? And how will Ireland navigate an increasingly unpredictable world? Former EU Ambassador to the United States David O’Sullivan joins Irish American attorney and political commentator Larry Donnelly, journalist and commentator Larissa Nolan, and political satirist Paddy Cullivan for what promises to be an entertaining, insightful and spirited discussion. events.title: Who's Minding the Machines? AI, Media, & the Public
events.description: From the news we read to the jobs we do, AI is already having a profound impact on everyday life. Should we be excited, worried or a bit of both? Who is regulating it, and what happens when the machines get it wrong? Joining the conversation are Theo McDonald, Senior Producer at Web Summit and current affairs commentator; Elaine Burke, award-winning technology journalist and host of the For Tech’s Sake podcast; and Paul Hayes, founder and CEO of Beachhut. events.title: Sacred Cows: Climate Change
events.description: Climate change affects everyone, but are we having the right conversations about how to tackle it? Are farmers being unfairly blamed for Ireland’s environmental challenges? Is rural Ireland getting a fair hearing? And how do we balance climate action with protecting livelihoods, communities and the economy? Francie Gorman, President of the Irish Farmers’ Association, joins documentary filmmaker and researcher Kevin Collins, whose work examines energy policy, climate change and the real-world consequences of government decisions.
